seed: Objects of type `block` under action ACTION4 with touching neighbours [arm] show mixed outcomes: no_change x10, x x4. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a global object such as a counter, HUD element or legend, read as state. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Ring (player) moves y+/-6 on A1/A2 with the dashed beam (arm, w=1+6k). Blocks overlapping the beam are carried, blocks hit by movers are pushed in chains, and any blocked mover cancels the whole move.
A4/A3 change beam w by +/-6. An unhooked extend pushes the swept blocks; if the chain would pass x=48 the beam slides under them (this is the A4 no_change vs x outcome; the global-counter hypothesis was rejected because no counter object exists).
Hooked (tip == block.x+4): extend/retract moves every block on the beam. A blocked extend or a retract blocked by the ring lets the beam change size alone.
Tags: the next block, when hooked and alone on the beam, becomes collected, and the rightmost todo block becomes next. Unhooking reverts the tags. Clicks and A5/A7 are no-ops. Stateless.
Unconfirmed: exact bounds (block y>=2, block x<=48, ring y in [0,58], w<=43) and the rule for picking the next block when several todo blocks are candidates.
